title: Seller's Real Estate Condition Report
description: Rhode Island General Laws §5-20.8-2 requires sellers of residential real estate (1-4 units) to complete and deliver a written Real Estate Condition Report to the buyer prior to or at the time of execution of a purchase and sale agreement. The report covers structural, mechanical, environmental, and other material conditions.

required_actions.note: Must be delivered prior to or at execution of purchase and sale agreement.

title: Lead Hazard Mitigation Disclosure
description: Rhode Island has among the strongest lead paint enforcement in the nation. Under RIGL §23-24.6-1 et seq. (Lead Poisoning Prevention Act), sellers and landlords of pre-1978 housing must disclose known lead-based paint hazards and provide the EPA pamphlet 'Protect Your Family From Lead in Your Home.' Rhode Island additionally requires lead hazard mitigation certificates for rental properties.

required_actions.note: 10-day inspection contingency period per federal law (42 U.S.C. §4852d). RI enforces aggressively with state-level penalties.

title: Agency Relationship Disclosure
description: Rhode Island requires licensees to disclose their agency relationship to all parties at the earliest practical opportunity. Dual agency is permitted only with written informed consent of both buyer and seller. Designated agency within a brokerage is allowed under RIGL §5-20.6-8.

required_actions.note: Must be presented at earliest practical opportunity, before any confidential information is disclosed.

title: Closing Practice — Attorney Optional
description: Rhode Island does not strictly require attorney representation at closing, but attorneys commonly handle title examination and closing. Licensed title companies and lenders may conduct closings. The state uses both title insurance and attorney opinion letters for title assurance.

required_actions.note: Attorney involvement recommended for title examination and closing document preparation.

title: Coastal Property Hazard Disclosure
description: For properties within a CRMC (Coastal Resources Management Council) designated coastal zone, sellers should disclose potential erosion, flooding, and coastal hazard risks. Rhode Island's Coastal Property Guide and CRMC setback requirements may affect property use and development rights.

required_actions.note: Disclose CRMC setback requirements, erosion risks, and any FEMA flood zone status.
